question: What is the primary danger associated with the reuse of disposable syringes?

options.B: Rapid degradation of the plastic barrel

explanation: Reusing single-use syringes transfers microscopic traces of blood and infectious agents directly between individuals. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why do patients in many primary healthcare settings frequently request injectable medications over oral alternatives?

options.B: Injections are culturally perceived as more potent healing agents
options.C: Healthcare workers refuse to prescribe tablets
options.D: Injectables are significantly cheaper to purchase

explanation: Patient preference for injections is often driven by the belief that entering the bloodstream directly guarantees faster and more effective recovery. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is the single most frequent cause of occupational bloodborne pathogen exposure among nurses?
explanation: Sharp instruments breaking the skin barrier during clinical procedures account for the vast majority of occupational exposures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why are student nurses and junior clinical staff particularly vulnerable to sharps injuries?

options.A: They are mandated to recap all needles after use
options.B: Procedural inexperience combined with fast-paced clinical environments
options.C: Hospital management provides them with inferior protective gear
options.D: They handle more hazardous medications than senior staff

explanation: Developing motor skills under time pressure increases the likelihood of mishandling sharp devices. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h2)

question: How does the use of multidose medication vials create a risk for patients?

options.A: The medication expires faster when exposed to room air
options.B: Patients develop immediate allergic resistance to the preservative
options.C: Multidose vials always require dilution with sterile water
options.D: Sharing vials introduces pathogens if a contaminated needle enters the container

explanation: Using a previously contaminated needle or syringe to access a shared vial seeds the entire contents with microorganisms. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h3)

question: A community health clinic administers daily injections from a single multidose insulin vial to several patients using separate new needles each time, but without wiping the rubber septum. What is the primary hazard?

options.A: Excessive pressure build-up inside the glass vial
options.B: Cross-contamination of the vial contents via external pathogens on the septum
options.C: Inability to measure the correct dosage for the final patient
options.D: Immediate chemical degradation of the insulin solution

explanation: Even with new needles, failing to disinfect the rubber diaphragm can transfer surface microbes into the vial fluid. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which population group faces high occupational exposure to sharps injuries outside of the hospital clinical wards?

options.A: Informal waste scavengers and municipal handlers

explanation: Individuals sorting through mixed municipal waste are frequently punctured by discarded needles and syringes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h4)

question: What structural failure primarily drives community-level injection injuries in densely populated areas?

options.A: Lack of antiseptic soaps in hospital pharmacies
options.B: Improper segregation and disposal of medical waste into municipal dumps

explanation: When clinics dump infectious waste into general municipal refuse streams, community members rummaging through trash are exposed. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of placing puncture-resistant safety boxes directly at the point of care?

options.A: To comply with fire safety regulations in hospital wards
options.B: To allow patients to dispose of their own medications
options.C: To prevent healthcare workers from walking long distances with exposed sharps
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing plastic bins

explanation: Carrying used needles across rooms increases the window of opportunity for accidental stumbles and needlestick injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h5)

question: Why is the practice of needle recapping strongly discouraged in clinical guidelines?

options.A: It increases the risk of missing the cap and puncturing the guiding hand
options.B: It slows down the administration of emergency medications
options.C: It violates the manufacturer warranty on disposable syringes
options.D: It dulls the sharp tip, making subsequent injections painful

explanation: Guiding a needle back into a small plastic sheath requires precise hand-eye coordination that is easily disrupted. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the recommended immediate local first-aid response following an accidental needlestick injury?

options.A: Squeezing the puncture site aggressively to force out blood
options.B: Scrubbing the wound vigorously with a surgical brush
options.C: Washing the area thoroughly with soap and running water
options.D: Applying strong chemical disinfectants and iodine

explanation: Gentle washing with soap and water cleanses the site without causing micro-abrasions that could facilitate viral entry. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h6)

question: Within what maximum timeframe must Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) ideally be initiated after a high-risk exposure to be effective?
explanation: PEP loses efficacy rapidly as viral replication establishes; therefore, starting treatment within seventy-two hours is crucial. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h6)
